description: cross-cylinders-fuse's two cylinders with the second turned about its own axis to just past −90°, where its seam runs beside the crossing vertex (0, R, 0) and meets the first wall R·sin δ from it, δ the turn past −90°: a turn about its own axis is the identity on the solid, so the result is the Steinmetz union of cross-cylinders-fuse at every turn, 2πR²L − 16R³/3 and centrally symmetric. Arris fails here where it passes at cross-cylinders-fuse's 30°: Fault::Seam from the pave at the default −90.02°, Unsupported 'no closed form' for the two walls at the closed-form-band variant's −90.03°. Open CASCADE builds a wrong body in the same one-sided band, turns between −90° and −90.049° exclusive: volume, area and centroid off by a sliver linear in δ, stated in measure_differs (ADR-0015) (plans/seam-parametrisation-faults step 3)

analytic.measure_differs: the result is the same set of points at every turn and centrally symmetric, yet Open CASCADE's volume is 1.46e-3 (4.5e-5 relative) above 2πR²L − 16R³/3 at −90.02° and 2.19e-3 at −90.03°, its area 4.39e-3 and 6.58e-3 above, its centroid 3.8e-6 and 5.6e-6 off the origin — each linear in the turn past −90°, and exact again at −90°, −89.98° and −90.049°. The closed forms are cross-cylinders-fuse's, which Open CASCADE matches to 1e-10 at a generic turn; the inertia is the two cylinders' tensors less the bicylinder's (∫x² = ∫z² = 64R⁵/45, ∫y² = 16R⁵/15 over their common)
analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE reports 9/15, two fewer than its 11/17 at a generic turn: it loses the turned seam's two hits on the first wall, 3.5e-4 from the crossing vertices at −90.02° against a vertex tolerance of 1e-7. Arris keeps them: each seam still meets each ellipse once, so its counts are cross-cylinders-fuse's 10/16
